item.title: [Recap] Brandon Miller (CHA): Brandon Miller notched 28 points (10-of-19 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, one block and five three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Lakers.
item.description:
Brandon Miller notched 28 points (10-of-19 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, one block and five three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Lakers.

Fantasy managers have been waiting for Miller to snap out of his shooting slump for quite some time, and he may have done so on Tuesday. The Hornets wing shot over 50 percent from the field, and 28 points was the most he’s scored in a game since October 28 against the Pistons. Miller has been asked to create more looks for himself off the dribble, and it’s been a struggle. Miller is still shooting 35.9 percent from the field, so the buy-low window may not be closed just yet. Also, while he played 32 minutes, the Hornets shut Miller down at the end of regulation, leaving him to watch overtime from the bench.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Naz Reid (CHA): Naz Reid (nose) accounted for 23 points (8-of-18 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 11 rebounds, four assists, two steals, two blocks and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Lakers.
item.description:
Naz Reid (nose) accounted for 23 points (8-of-18 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 11 rebounds, four assists, two steals, two blocks and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Lakers.

The line Reid recorded against the Lakers was in line with what many fantasy managers hoped to see from him consistently in Charlotte. Unfortunately, things haven’t worked out that way, and Tuesday’s overtime loss dropped the Hornets to 4-10. Making matters worse for Reid was an inadvertent elbow from Collin Sexton that he took to the nose late in overtime. He was subbed out and did not return. With Coby White and Brandon Miller shut down at the end of regulation, the Hornets lacked the options needed to potentially force a second overtime.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Coby White (CHA): Coby White finished Tuesday’s loss to the Lakers with 19 points (6-of-12 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, three steals and two three-pointers.
item.description:
Coby White finished Tuesday’s loss to the Lakers with 19 points (6-of-12 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, three steals and two three-pointers.

Although White has played in each of Charlotte’s last seven games, the team continues to limit his minutes. He logged 26 minutes on Tuesday and, along with Brandon Miller, did not play at all in overtime. The injuries and minutes restrictions the Hornets have dealt with have a lot to do with them being the worst fourth-quarter team in the NBA this season. Down the stretch on Tuesday, White and the other Hornets failed to do much offensively, with even inbounding the ball becoming an adventure. Charlotte doesn’t play again until Friday, which may be a good thing for White.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Kevon Looney (LAL): Kevon Looney finished Tuesday’s loss to the Hornets with four points (2-of-3 FGs) and seven rebounds.
item.description:
Kevon Looney finished Tuesday’s loss to the Hornets with four points (2-of-3 FGs) and seven rebounds.

With Walker Kessler (leg) out, the Lakers turned to Looney to start at center on Tuesday. While the veteran center grabbed seven rebounds, he played only 17 minutes, and his mobility was an issue. With Sandro Mamukelashvili (3/3/2/1) shooting 1-of-8 from the field, Lakers head coach JJ Redick eventually turned to two-way contract player Carson Cooper. While his numbers (3/4/2 in 18 minutes) won’t jump off the page, Cooper’s contributions as a rebounder and defender were one reason why the Lakers were able to rally. Kessler is expected to be available for Wednesday’s game against the Jazz, so Looney may find himself out of the rotation once again.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Luka Dončić (LAL): Luka Dončić tallied 36 points (13-of-34 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists, one steal, one block and five three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Hornets.
item.description:
Luka Dončić tallied 36 points (13-of-34 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists, one steal, one block and five three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Hornets.

Dončić didn’t have a great night shooting-wise, going 5-of-16 from three, but he still posted a complete stat line. The Lakers’ star has scored at least 32 points in 11 straight appearances, with the Lakers going 9-2 in those games. With Tuesday’s overtime win, the Lakers boast the best record in the Western Conference, something few expected at any point this season. Dončić has played like an MVP so far, whether the conversation is focused on the “actual” basketball or the fantasy basketball.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Quentin Grimes (LAL): Quentin Grimes amassed 47 points (16-of-24 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, three assists, one steal and 10 three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Hornets.
item.description:
Quentin Grimes amassed 47 points (16-of-24 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, three assists, one steal and 10 three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Hornets.

Grimes had the best game of his career on Tuesday, and the Lakers needed it, trailing by as much as 18 late in the third quarter before rallying to win in overtime. Grimes scored 21 points in the fourth quarter alone, outscoring the Hornets by four, and his three-pointer with 1.7 seconds left forced overtime. Austin Reaves (heel) is supposed to test his injured heel on Wednesday before that night’s game against the Jazz, so we should learn more about how much time he’ll miss. Grimes, the first Laker other than Reaves, Luka Dončić or LeBron James to record a 30-point game since Dalton Knecht did in March 2025, will start as long as Reaves is out, and he’s worth rostering until that changes.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Darius Garland (LAC): Darius Garland accumulated 20 points (5-of-15 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), three rebounds, seven assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Jazz.
item.description:
Darius Garland accumulated 20 points (5-of-15 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), three rebounds, seven assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Jazz.

While Garland kept the turnovers in check, committing one, and recorded a full stat line, he had a tough night shooting the basketball. The Clippers guard was 5-of-15 from the field, a far cry from his 50.6 percent shooting for the season. The biggest concern for him in fantasy basketball has been the turnovers, so there’s no need to lose sleep over Garland having an off shooting night.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Rui Hachimura (LAC): Rui Hachimura amassed 20 points (7-of-10 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, one assist, one steal, one block and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Jazz.
item.description:
Rui Hachimura amassed 20 points (7-of-10 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, one assist, one steal, one block and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Jazz.

After scoring 24 points on 7-of-24 shooting in his previous three games, Hachimura needed a night like Tuesday, even if the Clippers were on the wrong end of a blowout. This was Hachimura’s second game this season with at least 20 points, five rebounds and five assists. Even better for fantasy managers was his 70 percent shooting from the field, a strong output for a player shooting 41.5 percent on the season.

item.title: [Recap] Mo Bamba (UTA): Mo Bamba finished Tuesday’s win over the Clippers with 15 points (6-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 10 rebounds, three assists, one block and one three-pointer.
item.description:

While his season-long fantasy remains relatively low, Bamba has been close to a top-100 player over the past two weeks. Rostered in 34 percent of Yahoo leagues, he’s worth rostering because Utah is so shorthanded in the frontcourt.

item.title: [Recap] Jrue Holiday (POR): Jrue Holiday accounted for 23 points (7-of-19 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, six assists, two steals, one block and five three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
item.description:
Jrue Holiday accounted for 23 points (7-of-19 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, six assists, two steals, one block and five three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Timberwolves.

With Deni Avdija ruled out, the Trail Blazers needed someone to step up offensively. Holiday was still used in a reserve role, but his 19 shot attempts tied him with Damian Lillard for the most on the team. Jrue finished with a full line, and he’s become a bit more valuable to fantasy managers since Ja Morant strained his hamstring. Jayson Kent started for Avdija, finishing with eight points, three rebounds, two steals and two three-pointers.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Donovan Clingan (POR): Donovan Clingan tallied 12 points (6-of-14 FGs, 0-of-3 FTs), 12 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block in Tuesday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
item.description:

Clingan wasn’t dominant against the Timberwolves, but he still thoroughly outplayed Rudy Gobert. The Trail Blazers’ center finished with his third straight double-double, and he’s recorded double-digit rebounds in five straight games. Add in the assists, and Clingan’s stat line may help compensate for the percentages.

item.title: [Recap] Damian Lillard (POR): Damian Lillard finished Tuesday’s loss to the Timberwolves with 25 points (8-of-19 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, one steal and five three-pointers.
item.description:
Damian Lillard finished Tuesday’s loss to the Timberwolves with 25 points (8-of-19 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, one steal and five three-pointers.

Lillard finished with 25 points, but his layup attempt in the final seconds, which would have given Portland the win, was blocked by Minnesota’s Trey Lyles. He’s scored at least 20 points in seven of the 10 games Portland has played since losing Ja Morant to a hamstring injury, providing top-100 fantasy value. Portland visits Milwaukee on Thursday in Lillard’s first game against the Bucks since being waived in the summer of 2025.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] LaMelo Ball (MIN): LaMelo Ball recorded 18 points (7-of-17 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), nine rebounds, two assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Trail Blazers.
item.description:
LaMelo Ball recorded 18 points (7-of-17 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), nine rebounds, two assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Trail Blazers.

After recording at least five assists in five straight games, Ball had two in the Timberwolves’ two games against Portland. The good news for the Timberwolves was that they won both games, but that low assist number was a surprise. Ball finished Tuesday’s win one rebound shy of a double-double, offering unexpected value in that category. Even with the recent low assist numbers, field-goal percentage and turnovers remain Ball’s biggest issues in category leagues.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Jaden McDaniels (MIN): Jaden McDaniels amassed 22 points (10-of-16 FGs), five rebounds, four assists, three steals, one block and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Trail Blazers.
item.description:

While McDaniels’ offensive production has been consistent throughout the season, fantasy managers may have hoped for a bit more from him in the aftermath of Anthony Edwards’ knee injury. He’s scored 20+ points three times since Edwards was injured in an October 26 loss to the Cavaliers, and his 23 points against the Trail Blazers matched his season high. That said, even with the scoring, McDaniels is still providing top-50 value in category leagues.

item.title: [Recap] Ayo Dosunmu (MIN): Ayo Dosunmu accounted for 30 points (11-of-19 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, one steal and seven three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Trail Blazers.
item.description:
Ayo Dosunmu accounted for 30 points (11-of-19 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, one steal and seven three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Trail Blazers.

He has recorded six or more assists in three of his last four games and is averaging 5.5 assists per game for the season. De’Aaron Fox (6/2/2/2) also struggled against the Pistons, shooting 3-of-10 from the field, offering even less value to fantasy managers than Castle.

Late in his return-to-play process, the Thunder center developed inflammation in the patellofemoral joint of his right knee, necessitating Tuesday’s procedure. item.description:
Nikola Jokić accumulated 28 points (12-of-21 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 15 rebounds, seven assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Suns.

The good news for fantasy managers was that Jokić recorded a full stat line on Monday, finishing with his 10th double-double of the season. However, he also committed seven turnovers, matching his season high in that category. By Jokić’s standards, he started slowly, but the Nuggets’ center has remained one of the best players in fantasy basketball, regardless of league format.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Jamal Murray (DEN): Jamal Murray finished Monday’s loss to the Suns with 28 points (9-of-19 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, two steals and one three-pointer.
item.description:
Jamal Murray finished Monday’s loss to the Suns with 28 points (9-of-19 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, two steals and one three-pointer.

Murray’s final stat line was boosted by a productive fourth quarter, as he shot 6-of-9 from the field and scored 18 points. That explosion helped the Nuggets guard avoid recording a poor stat line after a quiet first three quarters. And things won’t get any easier for Murray, as the Nuggets host the Celtics on Wednesday.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Miles Bridges (PHX): Miles Bridges recorded 16 points (7-of-15 FGs), eight rebounds, two assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Nuggets.
item.description:
Miles Bridges recorded 16 points (7-of-15 FGs), eight rebounds, two assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Nuggets.

While his numbers don’t jump off the page on most nights, Bridges’ consistency has made him a good player to have in category leagues. The Suns forward finished Monday’s victory with a full stat line, and he’s providing seventh-round value in nine-cat formats. Bridges’ fantasy ceiling may be limited, but the floor is safe.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Dillon Brooks (PHX): Dillon Brooks notched 15 points (6-of-17 FGs), four rebounds, four assists and three three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Nuggets.
item.description:
Dillon Brooks notched 15 points (6-of-17 FGs), four rebounds, four assists and three three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Nuggets.

After attempting two shots in Sunday’s loss to the Lakers, Brooks was far more active offensively on Monday. His 17 attempts led the Suns, and he scored 15 points for the second time in three games. At best, Brooks has been a late-round option for most of his career, with last season being an exception. Brooks is still rostered in 47 percent of Yahoo leagues, and Monday’s performance may have kept some managers from dropping him, despite the low field-goal percentage.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Jalen Green (PHX): Jalen Green tallied 16 points (5-of-10 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, three steals and two three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Nuggets.
item.description:
Jalen Green tallied 16 points (5-of-10 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, three steals and two three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Nuggets.

After struggling for most of the season, Green was efficient against the Nuggets. Shooting 50 percent from the field, he added value in multiple categories, including steals. Green’s three steals were a season high, bumping his total to 12 in 13 games. Even with the slow start, Green’s status as a starter is why he remains rostered in nearly 70 percent of Yahoo leagues.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Devin Booker (PHX): Devin Booker accounted for 20 points (5-of-14 FGs, 9-of-10 FTs), four rebounds, eight assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Monday’s win over the Nuggets.
item.description:
Devin Booker accounted for 20 points (5-of-14 FGs, 9-of-10 FTs), four rebounds, eight assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Monday’s win over the Nuggets.

After a brutal showing in Sunday’s loss to the Lakers, the Suns’ starters redeemed themselves on Monday. Booker didn’t shoot the ball well from the field, but the assist tally helped compensate for the low field-goal percentage. For the season, he’s shooting 47.3 percent from the field, so going 9-of-28 over the last two games hasn’t done much damage to Booker’s fantasy value.

item.title: [Recap] LaMelo Ball (MIN): LaMelo Ball struggled on Monday and finished with just six points (2-of-13 FGs), five rebounds, two steals and two three-pointers against the Trail Blazers.
item.description:
LaMelo Ball struggled on Monday and finished with just six points (2-of-13 FGs), five rebounds, two steals and two three-pointers against the Trail Blazers.

While it didn’t prevent Minnesota from getting the win, this was LaMelo’s worst game of the season. He set a new season low for points and failed to dish out an assist for the first time this season. This was an uncharacteristically bad performance for him, especially compared to what he’s done in the month of November. He was held to 19 points in their previous game, which was his first time scoring less than 20 points this month. He’ll get back on track in Tuesday’s rematch with Portland.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Rudy Gobert (MIN): Rudy Gobert recorded a double-double on Monday with 18 points (5-of-10 FGs, 8-of-14 FTs), 15 rebounds, three assists and two blocks against the Trail Blazers.
item.description:
Rudy Gobert recorded a double-double on Monday with 18 points (5-of-10 FGs, 8-of-14 FTs), 15 rebounds, three assists and two blocks against the Trail Blazers.

This was the fourth time this season that Gobert hauled in at least 15 rebounds, but he hasn’t had a scoring performance like this one. He set a new season high for scoring and scored in double figures for just the fourth time this season. Gobert’s still effective on the glass, and while he has improved as of late, he isn’t the shot blocker he once was. However, a huge dip in both field goal percentage and free throw percentage have really tanked his value.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Jayson Tatum (BOS): Jayson Tatum accumulated 32 points (11-of-18 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), seven rebounds, six assists and two steals over 30 minutes to lead the Celtics to a 131-94 blowout win over the Mavericks on Sunday.
item.description:
Jayson Tatum accumulated 32 points (11-of-18 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), seven rebounds, six assists and two steals over 30 minutes to lead the Celtics to a 131-94 blowout win over the Mavericks on Sunday.

Tatum put together a feast-worthy stat line just in time for Thanksgiving, exploding for 21 third-quarter points to extend Boston’s lead to 33 and effectively put the game out of reach before the final period. It marked the 10th time he has scored at least 15 points in a quarter, the most in Celtics history since the play-by-play era began in 1996-97, just ahead of franchise legend Paul Pierce. He’s delivered second-round fantasy value, averaging 26.8 points, 6.1 rebounds, 7.3 assists, 0.6 steals and 0.8 blocks through 12 games this season. The Celtics have won six consecutive games and will kick off a busy four-game week against the Magic before heading out west to face the Nuggets, Clippers and Warriors.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Cooper Flagg (DAL): Cooper Flagg tallied 17 points (5-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block over 27 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Celtics.
item.description:
Cooper Flagg tallied 17 points (5-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block over 27 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Celtics.

The Maine native did some real damage in the fourth quarter once the Celtics had already put the game away. It may have been garbage time, but it counts all the same for fantasy purposes. Simply put, Dallas looked like a completely different offense without primary initiator Kyrie Irving at point guard as he sat out the second night of a back-to-back in this one. The 19-year-old phenom has cooled off a bit over the last week, but he’s still averaging 23.5 points, 6.7 rebounds, 6.2 assists, 1.9 steals and 0.8 blocks through 13 games as one of the most impactful all-around contributors in fantasy. The Mavericks have a three-game week on tap that features showdowns against the Warriors, Clippers and Jazz.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Derrick White (BOS): Derrick White notched 16 points (6-of-11 FGs), four rebounds, two assists and two steals over 23 minutes in Sunday’s win over the Mavericks.
item.description:
Derrick White notched 16 points (6-of-11 FGs), four rebounds, two assists and two steals over 23 minutes in Sunday’s win over the Mavericks.

He didn’t end up with a block, but did come away with a pair of thefts as he was able to sit out nearly the entire second half as Boston built a massive lead, enabling them to cruise to the finish line. item.description:
Tyrese Proctor recorded a triple-double with a team-high 24 points (10-of-19 FGs), 11 rebounds and 10 assists to lead the Cavaliers to a 127-117 win over the Mavericks on Saturday.

The Cavaliers were without their entire starting five on the second night of a back-to-back, with nationwide travel disruptions on Friday contributing to a lengthy list of absences. Donovan Mitchell (knee), James Harden (calf), Peyton Watson (hamstring) and Jarrett Allen (knee) were all ruled out, while Evan Mobley missed his second consecutive game due to a toe sprain he sustained earlier this week. Proctor stepped up to lead Cleveland to an unexpected win by shooting over 50 percent from the floor, including 4-of-13 from three-point range. It was his first career triple-double. item.title: [Recap] Zion Williamson (NOP): Zion Williamson led the Pelicans with 24 points (9-of-16 FGs, 4-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, two assists, two blocks and two three-pointers in a 116-108 loss to the Nuggets on Saturday.
item.description:

item.title: [Recap] Yves Missi (NOP): Yves Missi returned to the lineup on Saturday and contributed three points (1-of-4 FGs, 1-of-4 FTs), eight rebounds, one assist and four blocks against the Nuggets.
item.description:

item.title: [Recap] Christian Braun (DEN): Christian Braun finished with 17 points (6-of-14 FGs), seven rebounds, one assist, four steals, one block and one three-pointer against the Pelicans on Saturday.

Christian Braun finished with 17 points (6-of-14 FGs), seven rebounds, one assist, four steals, one block and one three-pointer against the Pelicans on Saturday.

item.title: [Recap] Jamal Murray (DEN): Jamal Murray lit up the Pelicans with 23 points (9-of-16 FGs), seven rebounds, nine assists and two blocks on Saturday.

item.title: [Recap] Nikola Jokić (DEN): Nikola Jokić led the Nuggets with 26 points (9-of-14 FGs), eight rebounds, 10 assists, three steals and one three-pointer in a 116-108 win over the Pelicans on Saturday.
item.description:
Nikola Jokić led the Nuggets with 26 points (9-of-14 FGs), eight rebounds, 10 assists, three steals and one three-pointer in a 116-108 win over the Pelicans on Saturday.

It was a slow start to the year for Jokić, but he is starting to pick things up, especially over the last three games, where he has averaged 26.0 points, 11.7 rebounds and 9.0 assists per game while shooting 58.8 percent from the floor. The main improvement has been in his shooting percentage, as he is still at 51 percent on the season, which is well below his mark in recent years. This was the third time they’ve played the Pelicans this season, and while they did win all three, this was the only game where Jokić didn’t finish with a triple-double.
